name: Autocast

name: Diplomacy Deception (Peskov et al. 2020 ACL)
latest_version: Latest/canonical; still the standard reference. Follow-on work (Wongkamjan et al., ACL Findings 2025, counterfactual RL deception detection) reuses this same annotated corpus rather than releasing a new dataset.
size: train.jsonl ~2.47MB, validation.jsonl ~246KB, test.jsonl ~490KB (17,289 messages across 12 games)

messages: Hi Italy! Just opening up communication, and I want to know what some of your initial thoughts on the game are and if/how we can work together

note: sender_labels=true in the source data means truthful (self-labeled by sender); mapped true->option index 1 ('truthful').
review: ok
Good fit. The labels are real.

openjev.state: Diplomacy game 12, Spring 1901. Germany sends the following message to Italy: "Hi Italy! Just opening up communication, and I want to know what some of your initial thoughts on the game are and if/how we can work together". Germany's game score at the time: 3.

sender_intent.instructions: Classify whether the sender's message is truthful (sincere) or deceptive (a lie).

name: stanfordnlp/craigslist_bargains
latest_version: Static/archival, 2018 paper (He et al., arXiv:1808.09637). No 2025-2026 successor found; CaSiNo (2021) is the closest 'improvement' dataset but is not a direct successor and is itself 2021.

Description: Charge two devices simultaneously on the go. This vehicle charger with an additional USB port delivers enough power to charge two devices at once.

note: HF datasets-server refused this dataset (legacy loading-script format); traced the loader to its true CodaLab source URL (worksheets.codalab.org bundle 0xd34bbbc5fb3b4fccbd19e10756ca8dd7) and fetched parsed.json directly. Outcome/price fields present in the fuller record were truncated in the fetched sample, so labels are left null. | Converted to the Jev format: score 'final_price' bucketed into 5 ordered levels.
review: warn
The sample is cut short, so the deal and price labels are empty. The full record has them.

openjev.state: Craigslist negotiation scenario, category: phone. Item listed at $10: 'Charge two devices simultaneously on the go. This vehicle charger with an additional USB port delivers enough power to charge two devices at once. Auto Detect IC Technology automatically detects the device type.' Buyer's private target price: $7, no stated bottomline.

deal_reached.instructions: Predict whether the buyer and seller reach a deal, and at what price.

final_price.instructions: Predict whether the buyer and seller reach a deal, and at what price.

name: kchawla123/casino
latest_version: Static/archival, 2021 (Chawla et al., NAACL 2021). Positions itself as improving on craigslist_bargains and deal_or_no_dialog; no further 2025-2026 successor found.
size: 1,030 dialogues total (confirmed via HF API num_rows_total)

raw_sample.chat_logs_excerpt: Buyer: Hi! I need mostly firewood, how about you? Seller: Hi, I would like food and water most, I can give you all of my firewood. Buyer: That sounds great, I could use extra water too if possible!
annotations_excerpt: Hi! I need mostly firewood, how about you?

note: This dataset's HF datasets-viewer worked natively (Parquet). Full record also includes Big-Five personality, SVO scores, and per-utterance strategy annotations, omitted here for brevity. | Converted to the Jev format: score 'agent1_points' bucketed into 5 ordered levels; score 'agent2_points' bucketed into 5 ordered levels.
review: ok
Good fit. The point scores are real.

openjev.state: Campsite negotiation (CaSiNo) between two participants dividing Firewood, Water, and Food packages. Agent 1 priorities: Firewood=High, Water=Medium, Food=Low. Agent 2 priorities: Water=High, Food=High, Firewood=Low. Dialogue opens: 'Hi! I need mostly firewood, how about you?' -> 'Hi, I would like food and water most, I can give you all of my firewood.' -> 'That sounds great, I could use extra water too if possible!'

agent1_points.instructions: Predict each participant's final negotiation outcome (points scored, out of a max per-issue allocation).

agent2_points.instructions: Predict each participant's final negotiation outcome (points scored, out of a max per-issue allocation).

name: mikelewis0/deal_or_no_dialog
latest_version: Static/archival, 2017 (Lewis et al., arXiv:1706.05125). No direct 2025-2026 successor; CaSiNo (2021) is the field's next notable dataset.
size: 10K<n<100K (HF size category); ~5,808 dialogues in the 'dialogues' config

raw_sample.dialogue: THEM: i would like 4 hats and you can have the rest . <eos> YOU: deal <eos> THEM: <selection>
raw_sample.output: item0=1 item1=0 item2=1 item0=0 item1=4 item2=0

note: HF datasets-server refused this dataset too; fetched real first example line directly from the GitHub source's train.txt. Agent's output allocation item0=1,item1=0,item2=1 sums to 2 items received (used as items_received_count). | Converted to the Jev format: score 'items_received_count' bucketed into 5 ordered levels.
review: ok
The labels are real. The dialogue already shows 'deal', so predict from an earlier turn.

openjev.state: Multi-issue bargaining over 3 item types (books, hats, balls). Agent's private counts/values: book=1(val1), hat=4(val4), ball=1(val1); (count,value pairs: 1 4 4 1 1 2). Dialogue: THEM: 'i would like 4 hats and you can have the rest.' YOU: 'deal'. THEM: <selection>.

agreement.instructions: Predict whether the negotiation ends in agreement, and the agent's final item allocation (books, hats, balls).

items_received_count.instructions: Predict whether the negotiation ends in agreement, and the agent's final item allocation (books, hats, balls).

name: GTBench
latest_version: Confirmed current repo, paper NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2402.12348). No newer official successor under this name; adjacent but distinct 2025-2026 benchmarks exist (GameBench, LLM-Game-Benchmark) - not the same project.
size: Code framework covering 10 games (Tic-Tac-Toe, Connect-4, Kuhn Poker, Breakthrough, Liar's Dice, first-price sealed auction, Negotiation, Nim, Pig, Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma); not a fixed-row dataset
license: unknown (LICENSE file present in repo but content not read)
note: GTBench is an LLM-vs-LLM game-playing harness, not a static labeled dataset; raw_sample is a real YAML config file rather than a data row (no single canonical 'example row' exists). game index 6 corresponds to 'negotiation' in the listed options order.
review: bad
The sample is a config file, not a decision. You must run the games to get data.

openjev.state: GTBench game-theoretic LLM evaluation harness: Negotiation game configuration. GTBench pits LLM agents against each other or scripted opponents across 10 canonical game-theory games (complete/incomplete information, static/dynamic) to evaluate strategic reasoning.

game.instructions: Select which game-theoretic game this evaluation instance is configured to run.

name: TextStarCraft II
latest_version: Repo last pushed 2025-04-25. Direct successor: SC2Arena (arXiv:2508.10428, 2025) extends it with full-length contexts and full action space. Broader successor: DSGBench (see below).
size: unknown; live game environment/code repo, not a static corpus
license: none found (no LICENSE file in repo root)

raw_sample.content_excerpt: You are an AI trained in analyzing and summarizing StarCraft II games... 1. Information Overview... 2. Current Game Stage... 3. Our Current Strategy... 4. Enemy's Strategy... 5. Key Information... Finally, make {K} decisions from action_dict based on the current situation...

note: Repo is code/prompt templates, not a static labeled action dataset; ground-truth action left null. action option set is a representative summary of typical StarCraft II macro decisions, not verbatim from the repo's action_dict.
review: bad
The sample is a prompt template. The action options were made up and there is no label.

openjev.state: TextStarCraft II LLM agent prompt: the agent is given a game-state summary (resources, unit counts, tech, enemy scouting info) and asked to choose K actions from a discrete action_dict covering build orders, unit production, and military commands, given the current game stage and own/enemy strategy summaries.

action.instructions: Select the next macro-level action for the StarCraft II agent to take.

name: DSGBench (Diverse Strategic Game Benchmark) - 2025-2026 successor

Unified benchmark superset covering StarCraft II, CivRealm-style Civ scenarios, Werewolf, Stratego, Street Fighter III, and Welfare Diplomacy, evaluated across GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V2.5, Gemini-1.5-flash, Llama-3.1, o1-mini, Qwen-2.5.
